frozen_original.description_long: Michael Caputo’s July 14, 2017 testimony to the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence provides a first-person account of his work in Ukraine. Caputo said he lived briefly in Kyiv in 2007 and worked on a parliamentary election campaign for Bloc Lytvyn, founded by Volodymyr Lytvyn. He testified that the bloc ran against the party of then-president Viktor Yanukovych, which he said Paul Manafort managed, and that Lytvyn was elected and later became speaker of Ukraine’s parliament. The testimony supports describing Caputo’s consulting work and his account of the campaign. It does not establish that Vladimir Putin hired or directed Caputo, that the campaign served a Kremlin operation, or that it produced a political takeover. The episode also predates Caputo’s later work for Donald Trump, so it should not be framed as a Trump action absent a direct connection. The more dramatic wording relies on inferences the cited record does not substantiate.

proposal.description_long: A May 2026 report by North Dakota State University researchers assessed the effects of China’s 2025/26 retaliatory tariffs on U.S. agricultural exports. Using a structural gravity model, the authors estimated an annualized $14.9 billion shortfall in U.S. exports to China over March 2025 through February 2026, relative to a 2024 export baseline. The report attributes the modeled shortfall to China’s Fentanyl and Reciprocal tariff layers and estimates that soybeans account for about $6.8 billion. It also explains that the model separates tariff effects from other influences, including global commodity trends, exporter and importer shocks, seasonality, and monthly aggregate shocks. The figure is an estimate of China-bound export sales, not a direct measure of net harm to U.S. farmers. The report does not support the source record’s claim of a 72% soybean-export collapse. The AgEcon Search record dates the report to May 19, 2026, so this proposal treats the item as report-publication context and corrects the March 4, 2025 record date rather than presenting the later estimate as known on that date.

These are estimates of China-bound exports and a modeled tariff effect, not measured net losses to farmers or a 72% soybean-export collapse.
